I have grown cotton for 42 years, and on a farm this size with only two people in the household, I prefer a simple single-crop plan that I can manage carefully. Because I have well irrigation, I am willing to push for stable production instead of farming too conservatively. With my education and experience, I would choose improved seed rather than traditional seed, because I want better emergence, stronger uniformity, and more reliable yield without making the system overly complicated. I would use moderate-to-high fertilizer inputs: enough nitrogen to support vegetative growth and boll formation, phosphorus for root development and early vigor, and potassium to support boll setting and fiber quality. I would use plough tillage at the start of the season because I want a clean, well-loosened seedbed and better early root growth. Since I have irrigation access, I would plan several irrigations through the key growth stages rather than depending on rainfall. For pests, I would expect multiple applications because cotton usually needs active protection through the season, but I would keep it to the level needed to protect yield rather than spraying excessively. On this basis, I would aim for a solid, realistic yield rather than an aggressive target.
